items.text: Linux: middle-click pasting text selected in a block into a rich-text app (Tuta, Anki, ...) now pastes only the selection. Before, selecting the last line of a block (a one-line block, or Select All) also pasted the editor's own markup (`<div contenteditable="plaintext-only">`), the selection toolbar's button labels and the text of the blocks below (GH #530).

regressionEvidence.reason: Catalog coverage: UI-GH530-PRIMARY-SELECTION (fail-before proven; Linux WebKitGTK/Xvfb only, Wayland and Tuta/Anki not exercised). The unit test pins the placeholder that gives the textarea's shadow tree a trailing node; the native journey reads the PRIMARY selection flavours.

docs.reason: Restores the expected paste of a selection; no Guide page describes the X11 primary selection or what a middle-click paste carries, and no sentence becomes wrong.

Tap the block to bring the keyboard and the editing toolbar back (GH #716).

docs.reason: Guide gap filled in the release prep: the Platforms and mobile page said only that the bottom row gives way to the editing toolbar while the keyboard is up. It now says that closing the keyboard with Back or its hide key brings the row back at once while the block stays in editing, and that a tap on the block brings the keyboard and toolbar back (asserted in src/guideBeta5.test.ts).

docs.reason: Race fix with no change to any workflow or setting; the Guide does not describe when query results refresh internally.

items.text: Org graphs: a page you create from Search (Ctrl+K), with **Customize** for Today's sections, or by opening a page or journal that has no file yet is now edited as Org from the start. Before, until Tine next read the file, a property added to it (a block id from **Copy block ref**, a page property, a collapsed or heading flag) was written Markdown-style (`id:: …`) into the `.org` file, where Logseq and Tine show it as text instead of reading it as a property (ORG-CREATED-FORMAT).

regressionEvidence.reason: Catalog coverage: UI-ORG-CREATED-FORMAT (fail-before proven). The jsdom test creates pages the three ways named (Search, Customize Today's sections, an open page with no file yet) on an Org graph and checks the :PROPERTIES: drawer and #+key: line; the native journey checks the saved .org bytes after Copy block ref (Linux WebKitGTK).

docs.reason: The References page already says each property is written in the form its file uses (an Org page gets #+key: and a :PROPERTIES: drawer); the fix makes a freshly created page on an Org graph follow it. Bring-existing-graph says New pages follow Settings -> Editor -> File format.

items.text: A table, grid or board block that is the first block of a page and has its view set but no title yet is no longer rewritten as page properties when the page saves, so typing its title or adding rows no longer raises "Page-header properties must contain only valid key:: value lines" (often twice) or leaves the page unsaved. When that message is shown for a real page-properties block it now names the first line that is not a `key:: value` property (or says the block has child blocks), appears once however often you leave the editor, and is no longer shown for a block that is not the page's first block (GH #210). Choosing "Show children as: Outline" on such a block (which leaves its column-width settings behind) keeps it a block too, and setting an alias, icon or filter on that page no longer writes into the table block.

regressionEvidence.reason: Catalog coverage: UI-GH210-HEADER-TOAST (fail-before proven on 4e389bcfe: the render journey and the Rust test write the table block into the page preamble). Linux real-app journey e2e-page-properties.mjs; Windows/macOS/Android unverified.

docs.reason: Restores saving of a page whose first block is a table; the Guide never described the toast or the promotion, and no sentence becomes wrong.
